faq.q: How does the Tsawwassen North leasehold work?
faq.a: At Boardwalk, the developer states homes are purchased with a 99-year leasehold, presented as costing significantly less than a comparable freehold property; the homes sit on Tsawwassen Lands, where Tsawwassen First Nation is self-governing with jurisdiction over land management, so the lease documents themselves — not a listing summary — are the source to rely on for prepaid status, ground rent and taxes.

faq.q: Are townhomes in Tsawwassen freehold or strata?
faq.a: Most are strata, either a building strata or a bare-land strata, with monthly fees and bylaws. Some are freehold row homes with no strata. The title search tells you which, and it decides which costs and rules apply.

faq.q: What should I check on a townhome in Tsawwassen?
faq.a: Read the Form B, the bylaws, the strata minutes and the depreciation report, and ask about exterior repairs, pet and rental rules and who looks after the fences, roofs and yards.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Tsawwassen?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.
